1.text: Identify a person or an object
Use this pattern to introduce your role or identify an object. It connects a subject with a noun description. Keep it separate from statements about location or a temporary condition.
The ending changes with the subject. Identity statements use the होइन family for negatives, not the छैन family.
Change the occupation or nationality, then make a matching introduction and question.

2.text: Say where someone is and what they have
For a lost item or a meeting, decide what is located where. Place nouns take मा, while यहाँ, त्यहाँ and कहाँ already function as place expressions. Use सँग to identify the person who has something.
In a possession statement, the possessed item determines the construction. Distinguish मसँग ... छ from म ... छु.
Ask and answer about home, school or the market. Then ask the same person about one possession.

3.text: Use an adjective to describe taste, size or mood. Name the subject, give the description and finish with a form from the छ family. This makes the quality or condition the focus of the sentence.
With a person as subject, choose the appropriate form of छ. Do not confuse an adjective description with a noun identity such as being a doctor.
Describe two qualities of one dish, then try the opposite descriptions.

4.text: Compare a condition right now with something that happens regularly in a season or on a weekday. हुन्छ can describe a change or a general outcome. बन्नु is also used for becoming a profession or taking on a role.

rows: The market is closed on Sundays.
Not every day is the same.

4.text: Being cold now and getting cold in winter take different perspectives. भयो is one form used for a change that has happened.
Contrast now with generally for the same condition, then describe one change since yesterday.

5.text: Use location, recipient, starting point and means as separate building blocks. Nepali marks these relationships after a noun or pronoun. Practice one relationship in a short sentence before combining several.
Some pronouns change shape before a postposition. Distinguish म, मेरो, मलाई and मैले by their roles.
Start with a short sentence and add who with, where and by what means, using a friend, home and a pen.

6.text: Ask for the information you need

Decide what information you need: an object, a person or a place. Choose a question word such as के, को or कहाँ and put it where that information belongs. Do not rearrange the sentence into English question order.
At the beginning of a sentence, के can mark a yes/no question rather than ask what an object is.
For one shopping situation, ask separately about price, ownership, location and reason.

7.text: Match your wording to the person
The same message takes different subject–verb combinations with a friend and with someone you have just met. Learn the whole pattern rather than changing only the pronoun.
तँ is appropriate only in particular relationships. When unsure, use तपाईं and match it with a respectful verb form.
Make two versions of one question: one for a friend and one for a new acquaintance.

8.text: Use the present form for routines such as getting up, eating and working. Dictionary forms and sentence forms differ, so practice each verb with a subject.
Respectful forms follow a different pattern from ordinary endings. Remember to change the ending when you change the subject.
Describe three parts of your morning, then say the same things about a friend or family member.

9.text: Say what someone does not do
To negate a present action, change the verb form. Rather than adding an English-style not, learn the affirmative and negative as a pair for each subject.

rows: I do not work at night.

9.text: An action negative is different from छैन for nonexistence. Check the respectful negative forms as well.
Say one thing you usually do and one you do not do, then ask someone about both.

10.text: Use a progressive form containing दै for an action happening at the moment. Adding अहिले helps distinguish it from a daily routine.
Distinguish an ongoing action from a state left by a completed action. Do not add ले merely because the action verb is transitive.
Describe two actions happening around you, then turn one into a question.

11.text: Use the past form to report yesterday's actions or a single completed event. First check whether the verb takes an object. With completed transitive actions such as reading or writing, practice the agent marked with ले.
Do not mark an intransitive subject like the agent of a transitive action. Some verbs also change their stem in the past.
Make one sentence about who did what and another about who went where. Compare the subject forms.

12.text: Report an event that did not happen
Use a past negative when an intended event did not happen. Changing the past verb to a negative does not change the roles of the people, objects or places in the sentence.

rows: We did not watch that film.

12.text: The agent keeps ले in a negative completed transitive sentence. This differs from saying something has not happened yet.
Imagine two plans for yesterday. Report one as completed and the other as not completed.

13.text: Combine a present form with tomorrow, next week or another future time. Making the time explicit distinguishes a plan from a routine.

rows: We will eat at home tonight.

13.text: A definite plan and an uncertain prediction are different. Practice ways to soften predictions in the inference lesson.
Say one thing you will do tomorrow and one you will not do. Add when and where.

14.text: Use a habitual past form for repeated actions in childhood or an earlier period of life. Contrast it with the past of a single event.

rows: I did not use to exercise.
Did you use to live here?

14.text: Do not automatically copy the ले marking of a single completed transitive event into a habitual past pattern.
Name two former habits and then explain whether you still have them.

15.text: Describe experience and a present result
Use a past participle with a form of छ to connect an earlier event with now: having eaten, having visited a place or being tired after an event.

rows: I have not done this work yet.

15.text: Context distinguishes experience, completion and a resulting state. A negative can express not yet.
Choose eating, travel or work and practice experience, completion and not-yet completion.

16.text: Describe completion before a past moment
Explain what had already happened by a past moment. A reference such as when I arrived makes the order of events clear.

rows: I had not done this work at that time.
त्यस बेला मैले खाना खाएको थिइनँ।
tyas belā maile khānā khāeko thiinã
I had not eaten at that time.

16.text: Distinguish an action that was in progress then from one already completed then. This pattern combines a past participle with a past copula.
Imagine a meeting and describe one thing already completed and one not yet completed when you arrived.

17.text: Make a request that fits the relationship
Ask someone to do something. Start with a respectful request, then compare it with the shorter form used with a friend. The ending signals the relationship even when the subject is omitted.
A short form can sound forceful with the wrong person. Small particles after a request can also change its tone.
Say the same request to a friend and to a new acquaintance, then compare the wording.

18.text: Distinguish an offer to do something yourself from an invitation to act together. Short verb forms are useful when discussing food or going out.

rows: Let us play football, not tennis.

18.text: Shall I and let us use different persons. A suggestion not to do something places न before the verb.
Make one offer to help and one suggestion to do something together.

19.text: Ask someone not to do something
Distinguish a polite request to stop from a rule for a place. Choose between please do not and must not according to the situation.
Keep a negative request separate from a prohibition with हुँदैन. Neither is the same as saying an action is unnecessary.
Imagine a library or classroom. State one rule and make one polite request not to do something.

20.text: Combine an action with सक्नु to express ability or practical possibility. Put the action first and inflect सक्नु for the subject.
The action's ordinary present form differs from a can construction. Negate सक्नु to say cannot.
Choose language, transport or cooking and explain one ability and one inability.

21.text: Separate obligation, lack of necessity and permission. Use पर्छ for an obligation and पर्दैन for no obligation. Ask permission with an action followed by हुन्छ or मिल्छ.

rows: You do not have to pay.

21.text: Do not have to does not mean must not. In this obligation pattern, पर्छ does not change for the subject's person.
For a workday, state an obligation, something unnecessary and a request for permission.

22.text: Describe a wish or a passing desire
Compare a wish with a present inclination. A sentence with चाहनु and a मन construction with मलाई use different subject patterns.

rows: You want to go to Nepal.
He wants to go to Nepal.
We feel like spending time together.

22.text: Keep liking something separate from wanting to do it. Distinguish मन पर्छ from मन छ and मन लाग्छ.
Name one travel wish and one thing you feel like doing now, then add a short reason.

23.text: Make a noun description more specific
Place an adjective before a noun to identify a particular person or thing. For adjectives that inflect, practice agreement in gender and number along with word order.
Not every adjective changes in the same way. Learn feminine, plural and respectful patterns with actual nouns.
Choose one person noun and one object noun and describe each with two qualities.

24.text: Speed and frequency add information to an action. Notice which verb or adjective an adverb modifies, then compare ordinary descriptions with exclamations.

rows: We do not work at night.

24.text: कति can be used for an exclamation as well as a question. Consider the purpose of the sentence, not just its punctuation.
Describe one action with slowly, always and very, then add an exclamation.

25.text: When shopping or choosing a route, make the two options clear. Place भन्दा after the comparison standard. For a superlative, identify the group being compared when useful.

rows: He is shorter than his younger brother.

25.text: The best or biggest should have a clear comparison group. Do not add an English-style comparative ending to the adjective.
Compare two bags by price and size and briefly explain which you would choose.

26.text: Choose a connector according to whether you are listing, sequencing, contrasting or giving a reason. Decide how two short statements relate before combining them.

rows: He did not come because he had no time.

26.text: Confusing but with because changes the relationship between events. With पनि, also check what the word too applies to.
List two actions from today, then connect them as a contrast or as a reason and result.

27.text: Reading while listening and eating after washing have different time relationships. Compare a दै form with a form containing पछि and decide which action comes first.

rows: I eat after washing my hands.

27.text: Translating a sequence as while changes the action. Begin with two actions performed by the same subject.
Choose two simultaneous morning actions and two sequential ones and make sentences.

28.text: Explain the purpose of an action
Explain not only where you are going but what you intend to do there. Distinguish a purpose expressed with an action from a purpose involving a person or health.

rows: उ नेपाली सिक्नको लागि नेपाल जान्छ।
u nepālī siknako lāgi nepāl jāncha
He goes to Nepal to learn Nepali.
उहाँ आराम गर्नको लागि घर जानुहुन्छ।
uhā̃ ārām garnako lāgi ghar jānuhuncha

28.text: Purpose and cause are different. Check whether you mean an intended action or an existing circumstance.
Choose a library, a market or a friend's home and make two reasons for going there expressed as purposes.

29.text: Identify a person or thing with an action
Place an action description before a noun to identify a person or thing, such as the person who lives here or the road to school. Read the ने form together with the noun it modifies.

rows: This is the road to school.
पैसा पाउने बित्तिकै, उसले किताब किन्यो।
paisā pāune bittikai, usle kitāb kinyo
He bought a book as soon as he got the money.

29.text: Distinguish a finite present statement from a noun-modifying form. Adding बित्तिकै can express as soon as.
Choose a place, an action and a person and make a description that identifies which person you mean.

30.text: Make an action depend on a condition
Use this pattern to plan around weather or available time. Separate the condition from the action that follows and connect them with भने.

rows: तपाईं व्यस्त हुनुहुन्छ भने, म पर्खन्छु।
tapāĩ vyasta hunuhuncha bhane, ma parkhanchu
If you are busy, I will wait.
If you get hungry, please eat.
यो पिरो छ भने, म खाँदिनँ।
yo piro cha bhane, ma khā̃dinã
If this is spicy, I will not eat it.

30.text: भने can mark the condition even without यदि. Practice what happens when the condition is not met as well.
Use rain, time or price as a condition and contrast what you will and will not do.

31.text: Distinguish an impression, a tentative prediction, a possibility and a strong deduction. Let the ending show how sure you are instead of stating uncertain information as a fact.
पर्छ has different roles in obligation and deduction. Check whether the whole construction means must do or must be.
Describe tomorrow's weather or a friend's plans as both a tentative prediction and a strong deduction.

32.text: Focus on what receives an action
Use a passive when the window being closed or the letter being written matters more than the doer. Compare leaving the doer unstated with explicitly identifying the doer.

rows: We did a lot of walking today.

32.text: Do not interpret an impersonal expression such as having done a lot of walking as being forced to walk by someone.
Choose an everyday object and report what was done to it without naming the doer.

33.text: Use verbs for teaching, showing, waking and otherwise causing an action or state. Identify the initiator and the person affected as separate participants.

rows: Did you wake your younger brother?
She made me write a letter.
Father did not make me work.

33.text: Seeing and showing, or learning and teaching, are different. Learn causative verbs by meaning rather than adding an ending mechanically.
Use a family member or teacher as the initiator and explain whom they caused to do what.

34.text: Separate the speaker from the message. Quoted content may retain the speaker's original person, so check whose perspective is represented when translating.

rows: I said I was a student.
She said she had no money.

34.text: Said they would come and did not say they would come differ in the scope of negation. Match the reporting verb to the speaker.
Quote a friend's plan and practice reporting it to someone else.

35.text: Change the person and time while talking about writing a letter.
This appendix uses लेख्नु, to write. Starting from the stem लेख्, compare who writes, who wrote and who has written. The practice examples use the everyday situation of writing letters.
A writing event that did not happen

rows: I did not write a letter yesterday.
You did not write a letter yesterday.
You did not write a letter yesterday.
You did not write a letter yesterday.
You did not write a letter yesterday.
He did not write a letter yesterday.
She did not write a letter yesterday.
He did not write a letter yesterday.
We did not write a letter yesterday.
They did not write a letter yesterday.
I have done the write letters.
You have done the write letters.
You have done the write letters.
You have done the write letters.
You have done the write letters.
He has done the write letters.
She has done the write letters.
He has done the write letters.
We have done the write letters.
They have done the write letters.
That person wrote a letter yesterday.
I will write a letter tomorrow.
You will write a letter tomorrow.
You will write a letter tomorrow.
You will write a letter tomorrow.
You will write a letter tomorrow.
He will write a letter tomorrow.
She will write a letter tomorrow.
He will write a letter tomorrow.
We will write a letter tomorrow.
They will write a letter tomorrow.

35.text: Check the agent marker ले with completed transitive actions. Choose short imperative forms only when the relationship makes them appropriate.

36.text: Contrast identity, present location and a past outing in affirmative and negative statements.

Choose a form of हुनु according to what you mean. Compare being an author, being at the library and having been at the market the day before yesterday. Practice the subject and ending together as a short sentence.

rows: I am not at the library.
You are not at the library.
You are not at the library.
You are not at the library.
You are not at the library.
He is not at the library.
She is not at the library.
He is not at the library.
We are not at the library.
They are not at the library.
I was at the market the day before yesterday.
You were at the market the day before yesterday.
You were at the market the day before yesterday.
You were at the market the day before yesterday.
You were at the market the day before yesterday.
He was at the market the day before yesterday.
She was at the market the day before yesterday.
He was at the market the day before yesterday.
We were at the market the day before yesterday.
They were at the market the day before yesterday.
I was not at the market the day before yesterday.
You were not at the market the day before yesterday.
You were not at the market the day before yesterday.
You were not at the market the day before yesterday.
You were not at the market the day before yesterday.
He was not at the market the day before yesterday.
She was not at the market the day before yesterday.
He was not at the market the day before yesterday.
We were not at the market the day before yesterday.
They were not at the market the day before yesterday.
My notebook is in the bag.
Your notebook is not in the bag.
This used to be a library.
My notebook was not here the day before yesterday.

36.text: Use the हो family for present identity and the छ family for present existence. Past statements use the थियो family while retaining person, number and respect distinctions.
